title: build_tailnet_https_client does not call tls_built_in_root_certs(false)
description: In peer_fetch.rs, build_tailnet_https_client builds a rustls ClientConfig using .dangerous().with_custom_certificate_verifier(). The TailnetCertVerifier accepts any cert (network-layer identity from Tailscale). However the reqwest/hyper-rustls builder does not explicitly call tls_built_in_root_certs(false). The HttpsConnectorBuilder with .with_tls_config() replaces the verifier entirely, so system CAs are NOT used (the custom verifier is the only one). This is safe because the custom verifier in verify_server_cert always returns Ok. But it is worth documenting explicitly: a future maintainer switching from .with_custom_certificate_verifier() to a standard verifier should know system CAs were intentionally excluded. The comment says 'certificate is used solely for transport confidentiality, not authentication' but does not mention that system CAs are implicitly disabled. Same issue in discovery.rs build_probe_client and kith-peer TailnetCertVerifier.
